column1: # AUDIT NOTE, 2026-09-10 (clock NOT read; between 02:59 and 04:03), hand-written by A2AI-Orch. NOT a count line.
# The row `2026-09-10 02:26:18  88244a3  1897` WAS RECORDED BY A RED RUN: that
# run's 1-test gate exited 1 (scripts/no-change-dir-refs.test.mjs refused the
# brief linter) and 88244a3 was never pushed. The harness appended immediately
# after gate 1, so it considered neither the other five gates nor gate 1's own
# exit code, while the comment beside it called the recorded value "the last
# known-good one". Fixed (clock not read): the append is now deferred to the end of the run
# and happens only when all six gates are green.
# LEFT IN PLACE DELIBERATELY rather than deleted. It is superseded by the green
# 3c46e46 row at 1899, so it is inert; and the history is the evidence for how
# the ratchet has behaved, which a silent deletion would destroy. Had 88244a3
# been abandoned instead of repaired, this row would have refused the next
# honest run as a decrease 1897 -> 1819.
# AUDIT NOTE, appended 2026-09-10 06:15 by A2AI-Orch. THE ROW ABOVE
# (06:13:52  99b2112  1926) ATTRIBUTES A COUNT TO A SHA WHOSE TREE THE RUN
# STOPPED MEASURING SIXTY-ONE SECONDS IN. The run started 06:03:06 against
# HEAD 99b2112; c15e901 was committed to main at 06:04:07, while gate 1 was
# still executing; HEAD read c15e901 for the rest of the run and at its end.
# The delta itself is sound and independently corroborated -- 1899 -> 1926 is
# +27, and A2AI-Fable-Arch measured W3's record wall at 27 collected / 27
# passed on main -- and c15e901 adds one .md file with no .mjs/.json/.yml in
# its diff, so it cannot have moved a count. NEITHER FACT MAKES THE SHA ON
# THIS ROW THE SHA THAT WAS MEASURED.
# THE ROW IS LEFT STANDING, exactly as the 88244a3 row above it was, and for
# the same reason: the history is the record of what the ratchet did, and a
# silent deletion destroys the only evidence that it did it. Deleting a row I
# find embarrassing is how a baseline becomes self-ratifying.
# CAUSE, and it is a defect in the harness rather than in anybody's judgement:
# orch-gates-only.sh captures HEAD_SHA once, before gate 1, and NOTHING
# RE-READS IT. The final verdict printed "ALL SIX GATES GREEN at 99b2112"
# from a value read ten minutes earlier. A RUN THAT NAMES A SHA IT READ ONCE
# IS ASSERTING THAT A SUMMARY TAKEN AT THE START STILL DESCRIBES THE THING AT
# THE END. Being fixed now: an end-of-run re-read that refuses to call a run
# pushable if HEAD moved, and a GATE-RUNNING lock written as the harness's
# first action so a peer can see a run that has not yet spawned a process.
# NOTHING WAS PUSHED ON THIS ROW. The re-gate at c15e901 is the run that will
# carry a pushable verdict.
